The Ides of March

source_text: On 15 March 44 BCE, Gaius Julius Caesar was killed in the Theatre of Pompey. The conspirators numbered roughly sixty men.

On 15 March 44 BCE, Gaius Julius Caesar was killed in the Theatre of Pompey. The conspirators numbered roughly sixty men.

source_text:
Aftermath

Civil war followed within two years. Octavian took the name Augustus in 27 BCE and the Republic did not recover.
